items.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022
items.q: And we had to sit there — but he actually spent all the time doing this. We spent hours transcribing and talking with him to get the charts.

ctx.x: This is very interesting for me because I’ve played that song with different bands so to hear that thing and remember that I’ve played [scats]. That’s great.

You just never knew what kind of situation — I had another good one in mind, I’m trying to think of it now. Oh for instance — and these all ended up great records. James Taylor — we were close with him at one point, especially Barry was a close friend. And we did now I don’t know if I’ll remember the record. Of course Mike played on “Don’t Let me be Lonely Tonight” it had a wonderful tenor solo. “One Man Dog” it was an album. And James didn’t know traditional music writing or rhythms so he wrote the charts on…
I love hearing that kind of information because musicians, schooled musicians sometimes have an attitude, including myself for a long time, about we’ll call them “unschooled
